name: Camino Francés
description: The French Way of St James, 772 km from Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port over the Pyrenees and across Spain to Santiago de Compostela. The track links the stops; the Cruz de Ferro is placed along it.

sjpp.name: Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port
sjpp.text: Pilgrims get their first stamp here, at the foot of the Pyrenees.

roncesvalles.name: Roncesvalles
roncesvalles.text: Over the Pyrenees into Spain, an abbey and a pilgrim hostel.

pamplona.name: Pamplona
pamplona.text: The city of the running of the bulls.

puente-la-reina.name: Puente la Reina
puente-la-reina.text: An eleventh-century bridge built for pilgrims.

estella.name: Estella
estella.text: Near here a fountain pours wine for pilgrims.

burgos.name: Burgos
burgos.text: A Gothic cathedral on the edge of the Meseta.

leon.name: León
leon.text: Across the wide Meseta to the cathedral of light.

cruz-de-ferro.name: Cruz de Ferro
cruz-de-ferro.text: The highest point: pilgrims leave a stone brought from home.

o-cebreiro.name: O Cebreiro
o-cebreiro.text: Stone huts with thatched roofs at the gate of Galicia.

sarria.name: Sarria
sarria.text: Many start here: 100 km is the least for the Compostela.

portomarin.name: Portomarín
portomarin.text: A church moved stone by stone when the valley was flooded.

santiago.name: Santiago de Compostela
santiago.text: The cathedral square, the end of the Way.

alto-del-perdon.name: Alto del Perdón
alto-del-perdon.text: A windy ridge with a row of wind turbines and iron pilgrims marching across the sky.

irache.name: Irache Wine Fountain
irache.text: Next to the Irache monastery a tap pours free red wine for pilgrims.

san-juan-de-ortega.name: San Juan de Ortega
san-juan-de-ortega.text: A monastery in the oak woods of the Montes de Oca, founded by a saint who built bridges for pilgrims.

san-anton.name: Convent of San Antón
san-anton.text: The road passes right under the Gothic arches of a ruined convent.

monte-do-gozo.name: Monte do Gozo
monte-do-gozo.text: The 'Mount of Joy', where pilgrims traditionally caught their first sight of the cathedral towers.

story.meseta: The Meseta: wheat to the horizon, and your own thoughts for company.
story.stone: At the iron cross you put down the stone you carried all this way.
story.galicia: Galicia: green hills, rain and eucalyptus, and yellow arrows at every turn.

facts.shell: The scallop shell has marked the Way of St James for a thousand years.
facts.compostela: Walk the last 100 km and the cathedral gives you a Compostela, the pilgrim's certificate.
facts.unesco: The routes to Santiago are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.km-zero: Many walk on to Finisterre, once thought to be the end of the world.

cam-finish.name: Compostela
cam-finish.description: Walk the whole Way to Santiago.

cam-cathedrals.name: Cathedral Cities
cam-cathedrals.description: Reach the cathedrals of Burgos and León.

cam-wine.name: A Glass for the Road
cam-wine.description: Reach the wine fountain of Irache.

cam-dawn.name: Pilgrim's Dawn
cam-dawn.description: Make 15 commits between 5 and 8 in the morning: pilgrims set off before sunrise.
